title: Consumable Burn-Rate Spikes After Guests
dataSources: Consumable levels (`supply:level`), parcels (`delivery:parcel`), bin collections (`bincollection:event`), gift-card balances (`giftcard:balance`).
app: Household logistics feeds — smart-scale consumable trackers, parcel/delivery tracking APIs, council bin-collection calendars, and gift-card balance logs — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs and MQTT.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=supply:level guest_period=*
| stats avg(daily_use_pct) as avg_daily_use, latest(level_pct) as current_level by item guest_period
| sort - avg_daily_use
description: Compares how quickly staples are consumed during guest periods versus normal household rhythm.
value: Guests change consumption patterns fast, and learning those spikes helps you stock realistically for visits.
implementation: Tag supply snapshots with guest-period context; compare average daily use across normal and guest periods.
visualization: Grouped table of consumable burn rate by item and guest-period flag.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces how much faster household staples vanish when guests are around, so you can plan visits without running out.
